name: Stardust
tagline: A period tracker that pairs cycle logging with astrology, built around a privacy-first pitch.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The math here is not hard: a period tracker is a date log, a rolling average, and a prediction window, and an agent will write that correctly in an afternoon. Moon phases are a closed-form astronomy calculation, so even the celestial garnish is free. What you cannot one-shot is the part people actually touch daily: a polished phone app with home screen widgets and push reminders that fire without you opening anything. You also lose the written astrology interpretations, which are editorial work, not code. Build it if you mainly want a private log you control; keep the app if you want the ritual.
coreLoopDIY: A local-only web app where you log period start and end dates plus symptoms, and it predicts your next cycle, fertile window, and shows the current moon phase.
requirements: A browser, ideally installed as a PWA on your phone
Somewhere to keep the exported JSON backup, since there is no cloud sync
whatYouLose: A real native app with widgets and reliable push notifications
The astrology write-ups, which are human-written content and not something your build can fake convincingly
Breadth of symptom and mood taxonomies refined over years of user feedback
Automatic backup and restore when you change phones
Their public privacy posture and the audits and legal positioning behind it, which for this category is a real product feature
moatNotes: In cycle tracking, trust is the feature. A homemade log stored only on your own device arguably beats everyone on that axis, as long as you remember to back it up.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is in the habit, and habits live on the lock screen. A tracker you have to remember to open is a tracker you stop using by month three, and notifications plus widgets are exactly the part a self-hosted web build does worst. The astrology layer is also doing real work: it turns a chore into something people want to check, and nobody wants to write their own horoscope copy. Paying a few dollars for an app that nags you correctly is a reasonable trade.
notes: The prediction math is trivial; the reason you open the app every day is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first period and cycle tracker as an installable PWA. No accounts, no server, no analytics, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage, everything stays on the device
- vite-plugin-pwa for the manifest and service worker so it installs to a phone home screen

Data model:
- cycles: { id, startDate, endDate (nullable), flowByDay: Record of date to one of light|medium|heavy }
- logs: { id, date, symptoms: string[], mood: string, energy: 1-5, note: string }
- settings: { defaultCycleLength, defaultPeriodLength }

Features, in scope:
- A calendar month view: period days shaded, predicted period days shown as a dashed outline, predicted fertile window and estimated ovulation day marked distinctly.
- Tap a day to log flow, symptoms from a fixed chip list (cramps, headache, bloating, acne, fatigue, nausea, back pain, tender breasts), mood, energy, and a free text note.
- Prediction: average the last 6 recorded cycle lengths, fall back to settings.defaultCycleLength when there are fewer than 2 cycles. Show the predicted next start date with a plus or minus range equal to the standard deviation of recorded cycle lengths, rounded up, minimum 1 day. Never present a prediction as certain.
- A home screen showing: current cycle day, days until next predicted period, current phase label (menstrual, follicular, ovulatory, luteal), and the current moon phase.
- Moon phase computed locally with a standard synodic formula from a known new moon epoch. Render it as a simple SVG, no image assets, no API calls.
- A stats view: cycle length history as a bar chart, average length, shortest, longest, and the most frequently logged symptoms.
- Export all data to a JSON file and import it back. Put a visible reminder in settings that there is no cloud backup.

Out of scope, do not build:
- any login, sync, sharing, or push notifications
- astrology or horoscope text generation
- medical or contraceptive advice of any kind

Ship a README with install steps and a one-paragraph note that this is a log, not a diagnostic tool. If you need any config at all, read it from .env, but the intended state is zero config.
